forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: East Devon auditors need separate strategy to restore confidence in council accounts
news_drafts.lead: External auditors have told East Devon's Audit and Governance Committee they need a formal strategy to regain assurance over the council's financial statements. The committee will receive a separate regaining assurance strategy and capacity assessment alongside the external audit progress report. The development reflects wider strain on audit capacity: Grant Thornton's fee for auditing the council in 2025-26 has been set at £169,103, reflecting "increased work auditors must now undertake as well as the scarcity of audit firms willing to do this work." Planning delays occurred in July and August 2026 because of officer capacity to respond to audit queries, though auditors report being in a good position for the critical post-statement audit phase beginning in mid-September.
news_drafts.paper_title: External Audit Progress and Sector Update 2025-26

news_drafts.headline: East Devon faces permanent £3.8m budget deficit as government cuts funding
news_drafts.lead: East Devon Council faces permanent budget deficits of £3.861m in 2027/28 and £4.722m in 2028/29, driven by government decisions to cut funding allocations. These are not temporary pressures but permanent reductions in the money available to the council. The council plans to use reserves — money set aside — of between £2.7m and £3.9m to close the 2027/28 gap. However, the council's own financial strategy identifies that "the key risk is that short-term balancing decisions in 2027/28 create a structural problem for 2028/29 and beyond." The planned savings meant to prevent this remain limited. Planning fee reforms are expected to deliver £1.4m but are prudently assumed at £0.5m pending legislation due at year-end; a leisure contract renegotiation may deliver at least £0.5m.

findings.paper_title: Finance Report month 4 monitoring update Annual Treasury Management review 2025_26, 16/09/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: Reserves funding £1.8m Local Government Reorganisation costs (£0.5m internal, £1.3m external resources), expected to have no impact on General Fund position.
findings.detail: Cabinet is being asked to approve £0.5m of internal resources and £1.3m of external resources associated with Local Government Reorganisation, to be funded from reserves. The paper states these are 'not expected to have an impact on the Council's General Fund position'.
findings.matters: This is a significant one-off reserve drawdown; lenders need to see reserves are adequate to absorb such items without affecting core financial position.
findings.quote: A further report on this agenda seek approval for £0.5m of internal resources and a further £1.3m contribution towards external resources associated with Local Government Reorganisation. Both requests are to be funded from reserves and therefore not expected to have an impact on the Council's General Fund position.

findings.paper_title: Finance Report month 4 monitoring update Annual Treasury Management review 2025_26, 16/09/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: HRA business and asset strategy under review with potential impact on future outturn; affordable housing programme £5m on budget with 13 units under negotiation.
findings.detail: The HRA business and asset strategy is noted as 'under review which may impact future outturn forecast'. Concurrently, the council is on-budget for a £5m affordable housing acquisition programme; 13 units in Budleigh Salterton are 'currently under negotiation'. Funding is from 1-4-1 receipts, S106, and potentially additional borrowing.
findings.matters: Strategy review signals potential changes to future capital plans or borrowing; the active acquisition pipeline shows near-term deployment of housing resources.
findings.figures: £5m affordable housing forecast spend; 13 units under negotiation; funding from 1-4-1 receipts, S106, and potential borrowing
findings.quote: The HRA business and asset strategy is under review which may impact future outturn forecast. In the meantime the purchase of 13 affordable homes in Budleigh Salterton is currently under negotiation.

findings.paper_title: Finance Report month 4 monitoring update Annual Treasury Management review 2025_26, 16/09/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: Place Repairs and Recycling overspent by £170k due to bank holidays and rising fleet fuel costs; high scenario impact would be £265k.
findings.detail: Place Repairs and Recycling shows £170k adverse variance attributed to 'in-year Bank Holidays & unforeseen rising Fleet Fuel costs'. The paper notes this reflects 'medium scenario disruption work previously completed', with high scenario impact (35% uplift) reaching £265k. Fleet costs are explicitly tracked as a material pressure.
findings.matters: Fuel cost inflation is a sector-wide pressure; the council is explicitly tracking it with downside scenarios, signalling both awareness and potential for further deterioration.
findings.quote: Place - R&R – incurred costs due to in-year Bank Holidays & unforeseen rising Fleet Fuel costs. This is in line with medium scenario disruption work previously completed, high scenario at 35% = £265k.

findings.paper_title: Finance Report month 4 monitoring update Annual Treasury Management review 2025_26, 16/09/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: Treasury investment income forecast £266k above budget, driven by performance of in-house and externally managed funds totalling c.£51.1m.
findings.detail: Treasury investment income is forecast £266k above budget. Holdings at mid-August comprise DMADF £11m, Money Market Funds £9m, Payden Sterling Reserve Fund £15.437m, and Royal London Asset Management Fund £15.666m (total c.£51.1m). The paper notes this forecast will be refined as cash flow analysis is completed.
findings.matters: Treasury income outperformance is a buffer to financial pressures; it signals either good yield management or higher prevailing rates.
findings.figures: £266k above budget; holdings DMADF £11m, MMF £9m, Payden £15.437m, Royal London £15.666m

findings.paper_title: Finance Report month 4 monitoring update Annual Treasury Management review 2025_26, 16/09/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: General Fund balance forecast to draw down by £260k to £4.540m at 31 March 2027, from opening balance of £4.800m, remaining in line with approved policy.
findings.detail: General Fund balance is forecast to decline from £4.800m (1 April 2026) to £4.540m (31 March 2027), representing a drawdown of £260k. This reflects approved planned use of £300k offset by a £40k favourable variance elsewhere. The balance remains at approved policy levels.
findings.matters: Reserve levels and movements determine financial resilience; a planned, modest drawdown with balance maintained at approved levels signals financial stability.
findings.figures: Opening GF balance £4.800m; closing forecast £4.540m; approved drawdown £300k less favourable variance £40k
